title: Fix gamma_flip/max_pain artifacts + stale-IV hygiene in GexDashboard.py (issue #1)
scope:
Fix repo issue #1. Bug evidence (TSM packet 2026-10-15, spot 422.05, total net GEX -52.6M): market_snapshot.nearest_gamma_flip=430 (correct — aggregated strike data crosses sign at 430) but per-expiry gamma_flip values are 370/230/250/310 (artifacts), and several max_pain values are 225-235 (far from tradable range). Deep-wing strikes carry stale impliedVolatility of 300-450%.

ROOT CAUSES:
- compute_gamma_flip(df) scans strikes ascending and returns the FIRST negative->positive gex crossing. Deep-OTM strikes have noise-level gex (~1e-12) from stale quotes, so the 'flip' lands on a meaningless strike.
- compute_max_pain(df) evaluates ALL strikes unbounded — massive far-OTM put OI (e.g. 10,640 @ 270) drags the result far below spot.
- Stale wing IVs pass into the ai_packet strikes unflagged.

REQUIRED CHANGES (GexDashboard.py):
1. compute_gamma_flip: add optional `spot` param (keep signature backward-compatible: compute_gamma_flip(df, spot=None)). Ignore strikes whose |gex| is below a materiality threshold (suggest: < 1% of max |gex| in that df). Among remaining sign crossings, return the crossing NEAREST TO SPOT when spot is provided; if spot is None, keep the ascending-scan behavior but still apply the materiality filter. If no material crossing exists, return None (honest) — never return an artifact strike. Update call sites (compute_gamma_flip(df) and compute_gamma_flip(sub) in build_ai_packet) to pass spot.
2. compute_max_pain: add optional `spot` param the same way. When spot is provided, restrict candidate strikes to [0.7*spot, 1.3*spot]; if that filter empties the candidate set, fall back to all strikes. Update call sites to pass spot.
3. In build_ai_packet strike_objects: strikes with implied_volatility > 2.0 (200%, stale quote) must keep OI/GEX fields but get implied_volatility replaced by None and a 'stale_iv': true flag added; normal strikes keep their value. Document the flag in the packet (e.g. a data_quality note in meta or instructions).
4. tests/test_gex_metrics.py (new): must run OFFLINE — no yfinance/network imports. Reconstruct per-expiry DataFrames from tests/fixtures/TSM_ai_packet.json (each strike entry -> a row; for compute_gamma_flip a df with columns strike+gex suffices since gex is precomputed per strike; for compute_max_pain reconstruct call/put rows from call_oi/put_oi). REQUIRED assertions: (a) expiry 2026-10-16 flip in [425.0, 435.0]; (b) expiries with no material sign crossing return None (not an artifact strike); (c) every expiry max_pain within [0.7*422.05, 1.3*422.05]; (d) aggregated whole-book flip in [425.0, 435.0]; (e) synthetic edge cases: empty df -> None, all-negative -> None, all-positive -> None; (f) stale IV flagging on a synthetic strike with iv=3.5.
5. NO yfinance, network, or full-script runs anywhere in implementation or tests — market is closed and live fetches return bad data.
6. Keep code style consistent with the file (verbose spaced style is fine; do not reformat unrelated code). Do NOT touch VolumeProfileVisualizer.py, docs/, .github/, README.md.

title: Implement review amendments: absolute materiality floor, labeled constrained max_pain, IV/GEX provenance, extended tests
scope:
External ChatGPT review of the F1 fix returned NEEDS_REVISION with 3 blocking concerns. Implement these amendments. GEX units in this code: dollar-gamma in $M per 1% move (gamma*OI*100*spot^2/1e8), so a sane absolute floor is MIN_MATERIAL_GEX = 1e-3 (~$1k notional gamma).

AMENDMENTS:
1. compute_gamma_flip(df, spot=None): material strike iff |gex| >= max(0.01*max_abs, 1e-3). If max_abs < 1e-3 (whole slice is numerical noise) return None. Drop nonfinite strikes before grouping; zero-gex strikes never anchor a crossing. Keep spot=None -> first ascending crossing semantics.
2. compute_max_pain(df, spot=None): return canonical UNCONSTRAINED max pain as before; ADD bounded variant. Packet/dashboard output must emit BOTH: 'max_pain' (unconstrained) and 'max_pain_constrained' with 'max_pain_candidate_band': [0.7*spot, 1.3*spot], 'max_pain_band_fell_back': bool, and distinguish empty-band fallback from a minimum landing on the band boundary (e.g. 'max_pain_band_boundary_hit': bool). Name semantics honestly: constrained payout minimum, not 'nearest-to-spot'.
3. build_ai_packet: for stale strikes (IV>2.0) emit implied_volatility:null, raw_implied_volatility:<original>, stale_iv:true; document in meta.data_quality that stale-IV strikes' GEX is retained-with-flag (IV-derived gamma is suspect; consumers may exclude). Add meta.metric_definitions noting gamma_flip is a strike-profile sign-crossing proxy at current spot (modeled call-long/put-short convention), not the repriced-chain flip; max_pain_constrained defined as constrained payout minimum.
4. tests/test_gex_metrics.py: add cases - alternating +/-1e-12 noise -> None; all-zero book -> None; below/at/above the 1e-3 floor boundary; multiple crossings -> nearest to spot; unconstrained max pain outside band -> both fields + flags set; empty-band fallback vs boundary-hit distinguished; nonfinite strikes dropped; raw_implied_volatility provenance present; all offline (fixture only, no network).

HARD RULES: no yfinance/network calls; do not run the full scripts; minimal diffs; keep backward-compatible signatures.

title: Fix true max_pain root cause (NaN OI argmin hijack) + band-edge selection flag
scope:
External review round 3 caught that band removal alone cannot explain max_pain 225-235 -> 435, since the original compute_max_pain was ALREADY the canonical unconstrained payout argmin. ORCHESTRATOR FORENSICS (verified): reconstructing the TSM fixture df with exported OI=0 treated as NaN makes the ORIGINAL algorithm return exactly the reported artifacts 225/230/235 on expiries 10-23/10-30/11-27. ROOT CAUSE: yfinance emits NaN openInterest on dead strikes; pain sums become NaN; np.argmin silently returns the FIRST NaN index = lowest strike. Packet export collapsed NaN->0 via groupby().sum(), hiding it in the fixture.

REQUIRED:
1. compute_max_pain / compute_max_pain_constrained (and _payout_pain): exclude rows with nonfinite openInterest (and nonfinite strike) BEFORE the payout loop — document that a zero/nonfinite OI row cannot anchor a minimum. Add a regression test: df containing NaN-OI rows must return the true argmin computed independently, NOT the first-NaN (lowest) strike. State in test docstring that this reproduces the original 225/230/235 artifact mechanism.
2. Band-edge flag (minor concern): band_boundary_hit uses literal strike==edge equality, which misses constraint-driven endpoint selection when no listed strike equals the band edge. Add flag(s) distinguishing literal edge equality from selection of the lowest/highest ELIGIBLE candidate (e.g. 'selected_lowest_candidate'/'selected_highest_candidate' or a single 'edge_hit' semantics covering both). Add a test whose band endpoints fall BETWEEN listed strikes.
3. Provenance: add a meta.data_quality note that exported OI may conflate true-zero and missing(NaN-collapsed-to-0) rows.
4. Keep compute_gamma_flip semantics from F2 unchanged; nonfinite handling already present — make sure gex max_abs guard also handles all-NaN->dropped edge.
RULES: offline only, no yfinance/network, no full-script runs, minimal diffs, backward-compatible signatures.

acceptance_criteria.expected: all pass incl. NaN-OI regression reproducing original artifact mechanism + between-strikes band-edge test
reconstructed NaN-OI df yields true argmin not lowest strike

title: Tolerate empty/all-NaN-OI expiries instead of aborting ticker
scope:
Live SPY run (market open, 2026-10-16) failed: expiry 2026-10-29 has 2 rows with ALL-NaN openInterest. compute_max_pain correctly raises ValueError on all-NaN slices, but the exception propagates and kills the whole ticker's dashboard+packet (main loop catches and skips the entire ticker). This is a robustness regression from the loud-failure design.

REQUIRED: per-expiry metric computation in build_ai_packet AND the dashboard plotting loop must tolerate unusable expiries. Where a per-expiry sub-df has no finite OI rows (or compute_max_pain/compute_max_pain_constrained/compute_gamma_flip would fail on insufficient data), emit explicit nulls for that expiry's metrics (max_pain, max_pain_constrained+flags, gamma_flip) and mark it in the packet (e.g. 'data_quality':'no_finite_oi' or a 'metrics_unavailable' flag) rather than raising. Whole-book metrics on the combined df still compute normally. Dashboard plots for such expiries may omit the max-pain/flip markers with a note. Add tests: an expiry df with all-NaN OI inside build_ai_packet yields null metrics + flag for that expiry while other expiries and whole-book fields compute normally; do NOT silently return artifact strikes.

Keep ValueError behavior of the raw compute_max_pain functions themselves (loud failure is intended for direct misuse); the tolerance lives at the packet/plot call sites. Offline only, no yfinance in tests, minimal diffs.
